rationale.conceptual: The underlying method is a textbook application of equilibrium molecular dynamics with the Green-Kubo formula. No novel algorithm or derivation is required; the paper explicitly gives all parameters (time step, run lengths, averaging scheme). The only nuance is using the specific Lindsay–Broido Tersoff parameters and correctly computing the system volume with the van der Waals thickness.
rationale.execution: The agent must build atomic structures with different strains/widths, run many LAMMPS simulations (at least 30 for the strain series, plus temperature and width sweeps), capture raw heat current output, compute autocorrelation integrals, and produce three CSV files. This is a multi-stage pipeline with scripting, tool orchestration, and post-processing, but no fragile external data acquisition.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing an equilibrium molecular dynamics (EMD) simulation of a zigzag h-BNNR using LAMMPS with a well-documented Tersoff potential. The method is standard (Green–Kubo thermal conductivity) and the paper provides a clear protocol. While conceptually straightforward, the execution demands orchestration of many simulations (multiple strains, temperatures, and widths), post-processing of heat current data, and correct averaging. Overall a moderate engineering challenge but not conceptually deep.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The system size is tiny (10 nm × 3 nm ≈200 atoms) and all simulation runs are short (tens of picoseconds). The work is purely CPU-based; memory and storage requirements are negligible.
